\]

Thanks, that helps. Now I want to figure out: How many packs of glue sticks does Mr. Jackson need to buy so every student can have 2 glue sticks? By the way, here are some relevant details: Mr. Jackson wants to give each student 2 glue sticks. Mr. Jackson can only buy whole packs and expects to have some extra glue sticks left over.

1. Mr. Jackson needs:
   \[
   27 \times 2 = 54
   \]
   glue sticks.

2. Each pack contains 8 glue sticks:
   \[
   54 \div 8 = 6.75
   \]

3. Since he must buy whole packs, he needs to round up to **7 packs**.

4. Seven packs contain:
   \[
   7 \times 8 = 56
   \]
   glue sticks, leaving 2 extra.

\[
\boxed{7\text{ packs}}
\]
